lede: The biggest item this week is Monday's Town Council meeting, where a vote on converting two affordable ownership units at 215 East Colorado Avenue into employee dwelling units — removing the price cap entirely — will reshape how that housing stock works for locals. The School Board meets the same night to vote on resolutions backing Proposition NN and Amendment 87, plus second-reading approval of updated board policies. The County Commissioners hold a continued public hearing Tuesday on adopting new international building codes that will set construction standards across San Miguel County for years to come.

notable.stake: Board votes on state ballot resolutions and second-reading approval of two revised policies.
Resolution would remove price caps on two town-built affordable units, changing their housing-stock role.
Council votes on deed-restriction conversion removing affordable price cap from two town units.
Commission weighs leak forgiveness requests and a new fee that formalizes leak-check costs for ratepayers.
Subcommittee selects winter vendors for Gondola Plaza and appoints a new chairperson.
Continued public hearing on new building codes that will govern all future construction in the county.
P&Z reviews early-stage employee housing proposal at the high school site under an IGA with the Town.
